refs.quote: TNKase is a tissue plasminogen activator, indicated to reduce the risk of death associated with acute ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). ( 1 )
TNKase is for intravenous (IV) administration only, administered as a single bolus over 5 seconds. Individualize dosage based on the patient's weight (see Table 1 ).

regimens.dose_text: TNKase is for intravenous (IV) administration only, administered as a single bolus over 5 seconds. Dose ranges from 30 mg (< 60 kg) to 50 mg (>= 90 kg). In acute stroke clinical practice guidelines, 0.25 mg/kg IV single bolus (maximum 25 mg) is endorsed.

refs.quote: USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS === 8 USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS 8.1 Pregnancy Risk Summary There are risks to the mother and fetus from acute ST elevation myocardial infarction, which is a medical emergency in pregnancy and can be fatal if left untreated (see Clinical Considerations ).

hepatic.value: Liver metabolism is the major clearance mechanism for tenecteplase. No dosage adjustment in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment; use caution in severe hepatic impairment due to baseline coagulopathy.

mechanism_of_action.value: Tenecteplase is a modified form of human tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) that binds to fibrin and converts plasminogen to plasmin. In the presence of fibrin, in vitro studies demonstrate that tenecteplase-mediated conversion of plasminogen to plasmin is increased relative to its conversion in the absence of fibrin. This fibrin specificity decreases systemic activation of plasminogen.

value.speed: Administer as a single IV bolus over 5 seconds
value.dilution: Reconstitute 50 mg vial with 10 mL Sterile Water for Injection (SWFI) to 5 mg/mL
value.flushes: Flush line with 0.9% sodium chloride before and after (incompatible with dextrose lines)
value.instructions: TNKase is for intravenous administration only, administered as a single bolus over 5 seconds. Reconstitute with 10 mL SWFI. Dextrose-containing lines must be flushed with 0.9% sodium chloride prior to and following administration.

lactation_summary.value: There are no data on the presence of tenecteplase in human or animal milk, effects on breastfed infant, or milk production.

refs.quote: There are no data on the presence of tenecteplase in either human or animal milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effect on milk production.

value.effect: Tenecteplase remains active in vitro in pharmacologic concentrations, causing artifactual degradation of fibrinogen in blood specimens.
value.management: Follow specific precautions to prevent in vitro artifacts when drawing blood samples for coagulation and fibrinolytic assays.

refs.quote: During TNKase therapy, results of coagulation tests and/or measures of fibrinolytic activity may be unreliable unless specific precautions are taken to prevent in vitro artifacts.
